There are no derivations on this page. Folio 35v is essentially blank. What the image shows is faint show-through of the typescript on the recto (folio 35r, the page given as 'previous'). Three observations support this. First, the ghost lines match the recto line for line: 'Für n = 2 wird mithin F(α,β) = s's''/r² …', 'Bezeichnet man mit R den hiermit parallelen halben Diameter …', 'Das Resultat ist also für Kegelschnitte', 'Man kann allemahl diese gerade Linie so legen, dass s' = ±s'' wird …', '… die verschiedenen Theoreme.' Second, the circled folio number '(35)' also appears faintly at the left margin, as it would through the paper. Third, the page is a typewritten sheet, i.e. a later (probably 20th-century editorial) typescript copy, not a Gauss autograph. No ink belongs to this side. The only possible own-side mark is the top number read as '4.', and even that is doubtful (it may be the recto's '2.' seen through).

For context, the recto content (not on this page) is as follows. Take a conic F(x,y)=0 and a point π. Draw a line through π cutting the conic at P', P''. Let s' = πP' and s'' = πP'' (signed), and let R be the semi-diameter parallel to that line. Then F(π)·R²/(s's'') is constant, independent of the line's direction. Choosing the line as a tangent (s' = s'') or as a chord bisected at π (s' = -s'') gives special theorems. This is the classical Apollonius/Newton chord theorem, a conic analogue of the power of a point.
